newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Policemen seize control of Lesotho police HQ.
newsitem.headline: Policemen seize control of Lesotho police HQ.

text.p: Eight members of the Royal Lesotho Mounted Police, who are resisting arrest over the killing of three fellow officers in 1995, have seized control of police headquarters in Maseru, state radio reported on Friday.
The eight were reported to have rounded up several senior officers, including the acting police commissioner, and claim to have dismissed them.

They also said they will sack the commissioner of Lesotho police, Major General Bolutu Makoaba, when he returns to the landlocked mountain kingdom from Namibia, where is attending a Southern African Development Community conference.

Radio Lesotho reported the dissident officers are wanted in connection with the murder of three officers inside the Maseru central police station in October 1995. Attempts to have them arraigned in court have failed.
The dissident officers are claiming amnesty under Lesotho's Pardons Act which stipulates that security force members may not be charged for any crimes committed from 1993 to 1995.
State radio said a government statement condemned the officers: "This illegal action appears to have been taken as an attempt to further delay the appearance of the suspected officers in court."

Local news reports said the officers were also retaliating for the alleged killing of a junior policeman who had supported their refusal to stand trial. He was gunned down at his Maseru home last weekend.
